summary: Iteration 15 — PTZ + Apple TV pairing coverage. 15/15 backend pytests pass (auth gate on 5 endpoints; demo-mode presets/goto/patrol/move with correct simulated/logged/quiet semantics; slot=20->400; config-driven preset names; live-mode goto->424 with LAN-unreachable detail; ATV bogus-protocol->400; finish-without-start->400; start->404 with IP in detail). Frontend: Security tab (mobile 390px) renders ptz-controls, ptz-preset-{-1,0,1,2} with correct names (Home, Preset 1..3), patrol toggles 'Start patrol'↔'Stop patrol' with (demo) toast, ptz-dpad with up/down/left/right, zoom-in/out, experimental note — no horizontal overflow (scrollW=356<=390). Press-and-hold on ptz-up and preset click succeed. Settings drawer with camera.live=true & appletv.live=true exposes camera-apikey-input (password), camera-presets-input (text), camera-protect-user-input (text), camera-protect-pass-input (password), and atv-pair-btn-atv1..4; clicking atv-pair-btn-atv1 shows toast 'No Apple TV answered at 192.168.0.145' and button returns to 'Pair this Apple TV' (not stuck disabled). State restored to DEMO (camera.live=false, appletv.live=false, all protect secrets empty).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~1515 lines — well past 700 line threshold; splitting routes (PTZ, Apple TV pairing, auth, scenes, health) into router modules would help.
_ptz_run couples HTTP-mapping (import httpx) with log construction; consider isolating error-to-message mapping for testability and reuse.

ProtectPTZ keeps _session/_cam_ids as instance state on a module singleton; if two users configure different NVRs/cameras simultaneously (not expected on single-property wall tablet) the cached camera_id/session could leak. Acceptable for single-apartment design but worth noting.

PtzControls HoldButton uses setInterval 1000ms with a server round-trip each tick; combined with the server-side 1.5s dead-man _auto_stop this creates a benign but mild race (stop may precede the next move tick). Current UX seems fine.
AtvPair toast handling: on error after start(), setStep(null) is correctly called, so the button rehydrates to 'Pair this Apple TV' (verified).
test_credentials: PIN 1234 (also demo bypass while all devices live=false)
seed_data_creation: None persisted. During tests camera.live and appletv.live were toggled true, then reset to false; protect_api_key/user/password cleared at end. Final state: all demo.
context_for_next_testing_agent: PTZ: _ptz_run writes a UniFiPTZ command_log entry with status='simulated' in demo and raises HTTPException(424, friendly msg) in live when Protect NVR is unreachable. ptz_move is quiet (no log) unless stop. ptz_presets reads camera.ptz_presets CSV. AtvPair front-end expects atv-pair-btn-atvN inside atv-card-atvN cards which only render when appletv.live=true. SettingsDrawer camera fields require camera.live=true. Both are gated by conn.live in SettingsDrawer. Protect secrets (protect_api_key, protect_password, rtsp_url) are masked as __stored__ on GET and _unmask drops the mask on PUT so the stored value is preserved.
